mapped-utility.summary: Utility types are small mapped and conditional types from the standard library. Know exactly how each is defined, because their edge cases come straight from those definitions.
points: `keyof T` lists property keys; `T[K]` reads property types; `T[keyof T]` is the union of value types, and `T[number]` is an array or tuple element type.
`keyof (A | B)` is the shared keys only, while `keyof (A & B)` is every key. A string index signature makes `keyof` `string | number`.
Homomorphic mapped types (`{ [K in keyof T]: … }`) copy `?` and `readonly`, distribute over unions, and map arrays and tuples to arrays and tuples.
Change modifiers with `+`/`-`: `-readonly` makes properties writable, `-?` makes them required and strips the `undefined` that came from `?`.
Key remapping with `as` can rename keys and filter them out by remapping to `never`.
`Omit<T, K>` is `Pick<T, Exclude<keyof T, K>>`: it accepts any key and is not distributive, so it collapses unions. Write a distributive helper when you need one.
`ReturnType` and `Parameters` read the last overload; `Awaited` unwraps thenables recursively and distributes over unions.
traps: `Readonly` and `Partial` are shallow, and naive deep versions break functions (they lose call signatures) and arrays (elements gain `undefined`).
`Omit` on a type with a string index signature drops every named property.
A typo in `Omit<T, "nmae">` compiles silently, while `Pick` would reject it.
